reason: E2 directly supports the formation of an amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite with Ag and an order-of-magnitude wear reduction in TiNbZr-Ag, but it does not report friction reduction or validate the mechanism across the full RT–600 °C range. E1 concerns a 2D HEA nanoflake lubricant additive, not a bulk Ag-alloyed HEA, and thus does not support the key premises.
premises: Ag addition to HEA promotes in-situ formation of a lubricious, self-healing oxide nanocomposite tribolayer during sliding
The Ag-containing tribolayer reduces friction and wear via low-shear, self-healing surface reconstruction
This mechanism is effective across a wide temperature range (RT to ~600 °C) in ambient air
The TiNbZr-Ag alloy system demonstrates reactive wear protection with an order-of-magnitude wear rate reduction
